title: Blue/Green Swap Ops — Decision & Sprint Notes
content:
Summary:
This note captures the tactical decisions and open action items from the release-engineering bridge on 2025-02-13 where we validated the blue/green swap procedure for the next release train and codified rollback/patchback behavior for hotfix windows. Goal: reduce swap-induced user errors and ensure deterministic rollback in <5m for common failure modes.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Marco Ortega (release lead)
- Liang Chen (SRE)
- Riley Thompson (serving-runtime eng)
- SRE Oncall (rotating)
- Observability: Priya Rao (ad-hoc)

Top decisions (finalized):
1) Swap cadence: We will do blue->green swaps during the 02:00–06:00 UTC change window for this sprint unless an on-call exception is raised. Rationale: lower traffic and availability of engineering overlap with APAC.
2) DNS TTL: Set canonical CNAME TTL to 30s for the swap window (we revert to 300s after stabilization). All DNS changes must be automated through the infra pipeline to ensure parity.
3) Connection draining: 90s drain for persistent connections; we will rely on the L7 proxy KeepAlive + healthcheck tombstone rather than immediate TCP close.
4) DB migrations: no breaking migrations during swap. If a migration is required, we will use out-of-band schema change plan (backwards-compatible) and coordinate with product.
5) Rollback criteria (automatic): If 4xx rate increases by >150% over baseline OR latency p50 increases by >300ms AND error budget consumption >30% within the first 5m of traffic cutover, trigger automated rollback.
6) Patchback (hotfix) strategy: For critical customer-impacting regressions detected post-swap, we will prefer a hotfix to the green pool and re-run smoke tests before re-swap. Hotfixes that touch shared infra must use HOTFIX-98 followups.

Runbook checklist (to be used by release conductor):
- Pre-swap checklist (completed 20m prior):
  * Verify green pool health (all services: OK)
  * Confirm kv-cache priming for frequently hit models
  * Confirm autoscaler targets and surge capacity set (x1.5 baseline)
  * Validate synthetic traffic pass (end-to-end smoke)
- Swap step (0–2m):
  * Scale green pool to target capacity
  * Swap LB weights via infra pipeline (0->100 in 3 increments: 10, 50, 100) with 30s pause between increments
  * Monitor p95, error counts, and request-rate jump, call out if thresholds hit
- Post-swap verification (2–12m):
  * Run suite of integration checks: embeddings pipeline, stream responses, KV cache hitrate target >75%
  * Verify downstream queues and sinks (metrics, traces) are stable
- Post-mortem hold (if any anomaly):
  * Keep both pools alive for 30m while investigating

Telemetry & dashboards updates (owners assigned):
- New dashboard tile: "swap-quick-scan" (targets: p50, p95, 4xx/min, 5xx/min, cache-hit) — owner: Priya Rao — due 2025-02-17
- Alert tuning: Create a 5m rolling alert for 4xx spikes with 20s suppression for known noisy endpoints — owner: Liang Chen — due 2025-02-16

Open action items:
- Marco: update infra pipeline job to perform LB weight steps with proper logging and produce a swap trace id (RELENG-712) — due 2025-02-17
- Aisha: draft short runbook appendix for SRE Oncall with decision decision trees and quick-rollback commands — due 2025-02-14 (in review)
- Riley: add smoke tests for streaming API edge-cases that previously flaked post-swap (GH PR linked) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2418 — due 2025-02-18
- Liang: simulate DNS TTL propagation in staging and confirm 30s behavior across cloud regions — due 2025-02-15

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Long TCP connections from older clients will delay traffic migration and increase tail latency. Mitigation: drainage + L7 tombstone approach; we will also publish a short client advisory if we see elevated tail.
- Risk: Cache cold-start on green pool causing increased token-per-request cost. Mitigation: KV priming step and synthetic heat-up; Optimize will produce a buffer guidance for top-20 routes.
- Risk: Split-brain if the auto-scaler misreports capacity during the 3-step weight shift. Mitigation: require metric sanity checks before each weight increment; abort and roll back if discrepancy observed.

Decisions deferred / discussion items:
- Whether to standardize swap increments to 5 steps instead of 3 for higher granularity — Deferred until next retro; cost/latency trade-off evaluation required.
- Whether to make 30s DNS TTL permanent for low-latency customers — needs legal & compliance review (privacy/regulatory caching implications).

Quick notes from SRE run simulation (2025-02-12):
- Simulation run #7 caught a scenario where a dependent ML serving process held connections for 7m. We added a hard kill override in the staging script (Liam created a helper) but need to be cautious for production.
- Observability gap: traces for swap steps were missing trace metadata. Action: infra pipeline should inject swap-trace-id into request headers for downstream correlation.

Meeting attachments & references:
- Slack thread: #release-bridge (pinned messages)
- Test harness output: s3://release-sim/bluegreen/2025-02-12/run-7/summary.log
- Confluence: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RE/pages/2345/BlueGreenSwapOps

Next sync: 2025-02-17 15:00 UTC — 30m touchpoint to confirm infra job changes and dashboard readiness.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language in the runbook simple — oncall needs one-liners for rollback.
- Consider adding a "swap preview" dry-run that produces a timeline without executing DNS changes for stakeholders to review.

Unresolved questions (for product/infra):
- Who owns communication to external customers if swap causes degraded latency > 10m? (product / comms)
- Should we allow a single-service swap (subset of services) for faster mitigation vs full-cluster swap? Pros/cons need a decision matrix.

-- End of notes --
